Legal services / Tax law

GEO promotion for tax lawyers and tax advisers

Businesses seek tax advisers for specific disputes, audits and transactions. I examine which firms AI recommends for those needs, which claims can be verified and where the practice is absent from relevant answers.

  • Separate non-brand prompts for tax disputes and advisory work
  • Verify services, credentials and public evidence
  • Improve source pages and track comparable BMR results
Discuss your projectSee the industry method

Personally led by Alexey Yakovlev, GEO/AEO consultant

Selection barriers

Why tax law needs a distinct GEO approach

A generic promise to solve tax problems does not answer questions about a particular tax, procedure or business situation. The supporting information changes with the service.

01

Advisory and disputes are mixed

Tax planning, audit objections and representation in a dispute are different activities. A useful service page identifies their scope, documents and the provider's actual role.

02

Case outcomes lack verification

Claims about successful appeals or cancelled assessments need traceable evidence and permission to publish. One decision does not guarantee the same outcome for another taxpayer.

03

Procedural questions go unanswered

Prospects need to know what an initial consultation covers, how complaints are considered and what evidence to prepare. Descriptions should follow current tax-authority procedures.

Verifiable facts

Evidence behind a credible tax practice

I check actual services, professional roles, accessible publications and authorised examples. Regulatory descriptions are checked against tax-authority primary sources.

  • Tax types, appeal stages, client sectors and services the team really provides
  • Publicly verifiable analysis, authorised anonymised examples and qualified contributors
  • Confidentiality, decision dates, scope of representation and explicit case limitations

GAEO's existing law-firm methodology provides a starting point. No completed GEO success story for a tax-law practice is claimed here.

Scope of work

A verifiable GEO programme for tax practices

Start with buyer questions and baseline visibility, then develop accurate service evidence and remeasure the same prompts.

  1. 01

    Segment prompts and measure BMR

    Separate advisory, disputes, audits and transaction due diligence. Record baseline AI answers for stable non-brand query groups.

  2. 02

    Verify the underlying facts

    Review practice credentials, permitted disclosures, source documents and procedural accuracy.

  3. 03

    Improve site and publications

    Prepare a structured brief for focused services, profiles, procedural FAQs and sourced expert articles.

  4. 04

    Repeat comparable measurements

    Check the same AI services and prompts, separately recording mentions, correct roles and supporting citations.

FAQ

Questions about the service

Can GEO guarantee success in a tax dispute?+

No. GEO work seeks better discovery and factual representation in AI answers. Tax appeal outcomes depend on evidence and decisions by authorities or courts.

Must confidential clients or filings be named?+

No. Use permitted anonymised examples and public decisions. Taxpayer and professional confidentiality must be respected.

How are tax advisers and tax litigators distinguished?+

Describe the actual work: advice, compliance, audit response, tax appeals or representation. Do not attribute services or credentials that the provider does not possess.

How do you measure visibility for a tax practice?+

Fix a consistent set of prompts by tax type, business issue and geography, the tested AI services and the baseline BMR before comparing later results.

How much does tax-law GEO cost?+

GAEO's standard audit and monthly plans apply. Scope depends on jurisdictions, service areas, query volumes and source coverage.
